prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a low-speed head-on collision. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1122; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
- The repair labor hours fit the damage.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
text: Inspection of the front end shows a cracked bumper cover, a bent upper radiator support, and a broken headlamp assembly on the driver side, all in line with a frontal impact at low speed. The pattern of crush and paint transfer matches the collision as reported. Labor hours and parts listed on the estimate are consistent with this extent of damage, and the invoices contain no duplicated line items. Our records and the owner's account reveal no prior damage to this vehicle. Recommended repair: replace the bumper cover and headlamp, straighten or replace the radiator support, refinish the affected panels, and recalibrate the forward sensor after reassembly.
